Goal: I can construct a triangle's circumscribed circle.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Theorem: the perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle meet at one point, the circumcenter, which is the same distance from all three vertices.

Proof: a point is on the perpendicular bisector of AB exactly when it is equidistant from A and B. The point O where the bisectors of AB and BC cross has OA = OB and OB = OC, so OA = OC, and O is on the third bisector too.

The circle centered at O through the vertices is the circumscribed circle. The circumcenter is inside an acute triangle, on the hypotenuse of a right triangle, and outside an obtuse one.
